title: Scheduler path saturation leading to fallback oscillation — action tracker
creator: Asha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket created after a capacity/regression event where the scheduler path selection saturated on a small set of execution kernels, triggering repeated fallback decisions and oscillating latency spikes. This ticket tracks immediate mitigations, root-cause analysis deliverables, and engineering action items to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Between 2026-03-06 21:10 and 2026-03-07 02:40 UTC, customer-facing p95/p99 for text-gen endpoints increased by ~2x on Dedicated clusters in eu-west. A subset of customers experienced timeouts and increased token costs due to re-tries. No data loss, but several SLA alerts and escalations from two customers.
timeline: 2026-03-06 20:55 UTC: Canary alarm (p95 latency) triggered for cluster eu-west-2; on-call paged.
2026-03-06 21:10 UTC: Ops throttled new canaries to reduce load; temporary mitigation reduced overall tail but did not stabilize oscillation.
2026-03-06 21:40 UTC: Engineering identified high variance in kernel selection counts and repeated fallbacks to safe kernels following KV cache eviction bursts.
2026-03-06 22:15 UTC: Emergency config applied: increase KV cache warmup window and disable speculative kernel probing for 4 hours (rollback point recorded).
2026-03-07 00:30 UTC: Traffic smoothing policy applied (per-client token pacing) which restored stable latency for most tenants.
2026-03-07 02:40 UTC: Incident declared resolved for p99 within SLOs; post-incident analysis kicked off.
2026-03-09 10:00 UTC: Initial RCA reviewed — root cause hypothesis documented and validated against synthetic repro harness.
2026-03-11 15:30 UTC: This follow-up ticket created to track remaining action items and preventative safeguards.
root_cause: A confluence of scheduler path saturation and aggressive speculative kernel probing. When KV cache eviction spikes occurred due to short-lived high-concurrency prefixes, the scheduler quickly reassigned requests to alternative kernel candidates. The speculative probe logic triggered fallback to conservative kernels, then re-probed optimistic kernels causing oscillation. Lack of damping and missing lease/slot reservations permitted repeated churn on a small set of execution paths.
mitigations_short_term: Increase KV cache warmup window by 3x for Dedicated clusters (applied and validated).
Disable speculative kernel probing at the cluster-level during high-concurrency windows (temp flag: --no-spec-probe).
Introduce per-worker 'fallback backoff' state machine to prevent immediate re-probing for 60s after a fallback event.
Deploy traffic-smoothing policy for high-burst clients (Ops-runbook step), monitor for effect for 72 hours.
mitigations_long_term: Implement lease-based slot reservations to avoid path saturation when transient bursts arrive — design doc due 2026-03-20.
Redesign speculative probing to use probabilistic damping and exponential backoff tied to measured KV cache hit-rate and kernel-switch count.
Add scheduler hysteresis metrics and SLO guards that trigger automatic damping (canary then roll to all clusters).
Enhance our synthetic load harness to cover simultaneous KV eviction + speculative probe scenario and run nightly regression tests.
action_items: Liam Ortega: Implement fallback backoff state machine and unit tests; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4987; target merge 2026-03-14.
Priya Nair: Author lease-based slot reservation design doc and run review with serving-runtime team by 2026-03-20; doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/leases-slot-reservation.
Sergio Martinez: Extend synthetic harness with KV-eviction scenario and add nightly job; job config: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/synthetic-eviction-harness.
Ops (on-call rotation): Maintain traffic-smoothing policy for two weeks and collect telemetry; update in dashboard 'eu-west-2 latency - post-oscillation'.
QA: Create regression test that asserts no more than 10% kernel-switch churn under 95th percentile load; include in pre-release smoke.
acceptance_criteria: Sustained p95 and p99 latency < 1.2x baseline for two weeks under representative burst patterns (verified via synthetic harness).
No repeated kernel reassignments (>=3 reassigns per request) observed in production for 14 days after rollout.
Lease-based reservation PR merged and e2e-tested in staging with canary traffic shadow for 72 hours.
notes: We intentionally exercised a conservative rollback path during the incident rather than a full flip to older runtime to avoid further KV cache cold starts.
Next retro scheduled for 2026-03-18 to validate long-term mitigation progress and surface any cross-team dependencies.
